perProbe.query: how does uv resolve dependency conflicts when two packages need different versions of the same library
perProbe.comment: Top-1 is an auth-middleware test fixture about credentials in different indexes — completely unrelated to dependency resolution. The token 'different' (and 'realm') in the test name lured the encoder into the wrong domain. 2-hop expansion would not help — the seeds themselves are off-topic. NL-only query lacks any concrete identifier hint.

perProbe.query: where is the lockfile written to disk after a successful resolution
perProbe.comment: Encoder picked the lock-orchestration dispatcher (do_lock) over the actual disk write site (lock_target.rs::commit). Both are in the same directory but lock_target.rs is the only place that calls fs_err::tokio::write on the encoded lock. Wrong-granularity at file-level: right area, wrong sibling file.

perProbe.query: how does uv decide whether to download a managed Python build or use one already on the system
perProbe.comment: Right crate (uv-python), reasonable sibling — PythonInstallation does combine PythonPreference + PythonDownloads enums to drive find-or-download. But the actual decision logic (PythonPreference enum semantics) lives in discovery.rs. Encoder picked the type that owns the result rather than the file with the decision logic. 2-hop expansion would help if the dense seeds were wider.

perProbe.query: when uv installs a wheel where does it actually copy the files from cache into the virtualenv
perProbe.got: crates/uv-install-wheel/src/wheel.rs (lines 587-588, no symbol — install_data starts at 589)
perProbe.comment: Right crate (uv-install-wheel), wrong file. wheel.rs::install_data moves files from .data dir, but link_wheel_files (linker.rs:255) is the actual copier into the venv. The 587-588 chunk is also a 1-line span lacking a symbol — a chunker boundary issue stripped the function header. Within-crate disambiguation failure.

perProbe.query: how does uv know whether the uv.lock file is stale and needs re-resolving
perProbe.expected: crates/uv-resolver/src/lock/mod.rs (Lock::satisfies at line 1614) OR crates/uv/src/commands/project/lock.rs (do_lock at 469)
perProbe.got: crates/uv/src/commands/project/lock.rs (lock at line 85, the public CLI lock fn)
perProbe.comment: File matched (lock.rs), but the chunk picked is the public entrypoint `lock` (line 85) rather than expected `do_lock` (line 469) or `Lock::satisfies` (lock/mod.rs:1614). The staleness check is in `do_lock` — public `lock` only delegates. Symbol-pick within a multi-symbol file is the issue.

perProbe.query: how does uv build a source distribution into a wheel before installing it
perProbe.expected: expectedSymbolAnyOf:[SourceBuild, build, SourceDistributionBuilder] in source/mod.rs or build-frontend/lib.rs
perProbe.comment: The retrieved symbol `build_distribution` (source/mod.rs:2453) is an EXCELLENT answer — its docstring literally says 'Build a source distribution, storing the built wheel in the cache'. The probe restricts symbols to {SourceBuild, build, SourceDistributionBuilder} which is too narrow; `build_distribution` is the in-context orchestrator and should be acceptable.

perProbe.query: what controls whether uv compiles bytecode for installed packages and how is it triggered
perProbe.comment: Lexical token 'compile' is shared across two completely different concepts in uv: (a) `pip compile` (resolve requirements.txt → resolved set) and (b) bytecode compileall. The encoder grabbed the imports header of the pip-compile command file. Classic word-sense ambiguity — 'compile' in Python tooling normally means pip-tools-style resolve, not bytecode generation.

perProbe.query: show me the Cache struct definition
perProbe.comment: Right crate (uv-cache), wrong sibling file. The CacheArgs struct in cli.rs is what user-facing CLI flags map to; the actual `Cache` runtime struct is in lib.rs:164. Encoder collapsed `Cache` and `CacheArgs` because both contain the literal token 'Cache'. A file-name token reranker (lib.rs > cli.rs for non-CLI queries) or symbol-name exact match would catch this.

perProbe.query: show me the Resolver struct definition
perProbe.comment: `Resolution` is in the same conceptual family as `Resolver` (resolver outputs the Resolution). For a literal 'show me Resolver' definition query the symbol-exact match (Resolver vs Resolution) should outweigh prose similarity. Symbol-name exact-match boost would fix this.

perProbe.query: trace how uv add inserts a new dependency into pyproject.toml
perProbe.comment: no_results returned in 3ms — pipeline early-exited without surfacing any chunk. Likely cause: query has 'how' (a stop-word) plus 'trace' which is rare in source; after stop-word filtering and confidence-floor checks the candidate set was empty. Both `add` and `pyproject_mut.rs` are real, indexed, and well-named — this is a query-side failure, not a corpus gap.

perProbe.query: what happens end-to-end when I run uv sync on an existing project
perProbe.got: Dockerfile (lines 24-25, 'COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./' / 'RUN uv sync --only-group docker')
perProbe.comment: The Dockerfile literally contains `uv sync` and `uv.lock` tokens — a perfect 2-token lexical match overrode any source-file dense score. Sync.rs (line 60 entry, 633 do_sync) was likely below the floor or RRF didn't promote it. Multi-file-flow-failure: even with 2-hop expansion the source files weren't seeded. A file-extension or file-kind boost (Rust source vs Dockerfile) would prevent the docs/config flank from winning.

perProbe.query: how does uv tool install create an isolated environment and link entrypoints onto PATH
perProbe.comment: Right concept (ToolEntrypoint exists for the bin shims), but tool.rs is a sibling file in the same crate as the expected lib.rs. The token 'entrypoint' from the query directly matched ToolEntrypoint::new. The actual install flow lives in commands/tool/install.rs:55 and uv-tool/src/lib.rs (tool_executable_dir). Within-crate disambiguation failure — would benefit from rewarding files whose name better matches the verb in the query (install vs entrypoint).

perProbe.query: trace how uv lock decides which package versions to write into uv.lock
perProbe.comment: Like FLOW-1, no_results in 3ms. Same query-shape issue: starts with 'trace how'. Both `lock.rs` and `resolver/mod.rs` are heavily-indexed canonical files; the failure is in the query parser/floor logic that drops the request entirely. Possibly the same combination — 'trace' + 'how' + 'uv' becomes too thin after stopword and dedup, dropping below the candidate floor.

perProbe.query: where is the code that fetches a wheel from a registry index and caches it
perProbe.comment: Right crate (uv-distribution), wrong submodule. registry_wheel_index.rs builds an in-memory index of cached wheels — not the fetcher. distribution_database.rs is the actual cache+download wrapper. The query tokens 'wheel', 'registry', 'index', 'cache' all appear in the wrong-file's name AND content — perfect lexical bait. Encoder + filename matched the noisy file.

perProbe.query: trace how uv venv creates a new virtual environment from scratch
perProbe.comment: File matched but the chunk is the small VenvError enum (47-63), not the actual `venv()` async fn that starts at line 64. Within-file granularity issue: the chunker scored a small declarative enum higher than the long pub fn just below it. Symbol/type filter for 'fn' over 'enum' on flow queries would help. expectedSymbolAnyOf is `[venv, create_venv]`.

perProbe.query: how does uv publish authenticate with PyPI using trusted publishing tokens
perProbe.comment: PublishSettings::resolve only forwards trusted_publishing config from CLI args — it doesn't authenticate. The actual call site is uv-publish/src/lib.rs:409 `check_trusted_publishing`. Encoder picked the settings struct because it contains the literal field `trusted_publishing` plus the words 'publish' and 'resolve'. Settings/config files should be downweighted vs implementation files for behavioural queries.

perProbe.query: how does uv clone a git dependency and pin it to a specific commit
perProbe.got: crates/uv-types/src/builds.rs (a 3-line `fn clone(&self) -> Self` Clone impl, lines 69-71)
perProbe.comment: Catastrophic word-sense collapse: query 'clone a git dependency' matched a `Clone::clone` derive impl on a build settings struct. Three-line stub function with no real semantics outscored uv-git/src/source.rs::fetch (the real Git clone). Stub-impl demotion is in the codebase (commit ac280d4) but apparently didn't reach this chunk. Worth checking if uv-types::builds clone got tagged as stub.

perProbe.query: where is the ResolveError::ConflictingUrls variant constructed
perProbe.expected: crates/uv-resolver/src/error.rs (ResolveError enum, ConflictingUrls variant defined at line 67)
perProbe.got: crates/uv-resolver/src/fork_urls.rs (ForkUrls struct, lines 1-52, contains construction site at line 39)
perProbe.comment: The query asks 'where is the variant CONSTRUCTED'. fork_urls.rs:39 is one of EXACTLY two construction sites (the other is resolver/urls.rs:162). The probe expected the DEFINITION file (error.rs:67) but the query literally asks for the construction site. Top-1 is correct for the literal wording; gold mixes 'defined' and 'constructed'.

perProbe.query: what does PubGrubReportFormatter do when rendering a resolution failure
perProbe.expected: crates/uv-resolver/src/pubgrub/report.rs (PubGrubReportFormatter struct at line 37, ReportFormatter impl at 54)
perProbe.got: crates/uv-resolver/src/pubgrub/report.rs (line 354 only, single-line `impl PubGrubReportFormatter<'_> {` header, no symbol attached)
perProbe.comment: File matched but the chunk is a single-line impl header (just 'impl PubGrubReportFormatter<\'_> {' at 354) with no captured symbol. Chunker boundary issue: the impl block's contents were apparently not associated with the impl header. Should never produce a 1-line chunk as top-1.

perProbe.query: what error is raised when a wheel is missing a header file required to build a C extension
perProbe.expected: crates/uv-build-frontend/src/error.rs (MissingHeaderError struct at 337 OR MissingHeaderCause at 131)
perProbe.comment: File matched (right error.rs) but symbol is a #[test] function inside the file's test module that exercises MissingHeaderError detection. Tests should be downweighted for type/struct/enum queries. The test fn includes the words 'missing' and 'linker' which match 'missing' + 'header' lexically. Symbol-type filter for non-test code on type-definition queries would catch this.

goldNotes: UV-ERR-2 gold expects definition file but the query asks for construction site. Probe wording is misaligned with expected file.
UV-NL-6 expectedSymbolAnyOf is too narrow — `build_distribution` in source/mod.rs is an excellent answer that the rubric rejects.

topThreeFixes.fix: Symbol-name exact-match boost on definition-style queries (DEF + ERR-type)
topThreeFixes.rationale: Queries of the form 'show me X struct/enum' or 'what does X type represent' should give a hard boost to chunks whose symbol == X (case-insensitive). Would fix UV-DEF-1 (Cache vs CacheArgs), UV-DEF-4 (Resolver vs Resolution), UV-ERR-3 (anonymous chunk), UV-ERR-4 (test fn missing_linker_library vs MissingHeaderError struct). Generic and principled — rewards lexical exactness on a query class where it should dominate.

topThreeFixes.fix: File-kind / file-name reranker that prefers implementation Rust source over (a) settings.rs, (b) Dockerfile/configs, (c) test files for behavioural and flow queries
topThreeFixes.rationale: Penalize files whose role is wiring/config/CLI/tests when the query is about behaviour, not configuration. Would fix UV-FLOW-2 (Dockerfile won), UV-FLOW-7 (settings.rs::PublishSettings vs uv-publish/src/lib.rs::check_trusted_publishing), UV-DEF-1 (cli.rs vs lib.rs), UV-ERR-4 (test fn vs struct), and likely help UV-FLOW-3 (commands/install.rs over uv-tool/src/tool.rs). Generic: file-kind heuristics already exist in detectFileKind — extend the demotion ratios for non-implementation files when query has behavioural verbs (creates, fetches, authenticates, etc.).

topThreeFixes.fix: Empty-result rescue path: when token-filtered query is too thin to produce candidates, fall back to dense-only with the original raw query (no stopword strip), instead of returning no_results
topThreeFixes.rationale: UV-FLOW-1 and UV-FLOW-4 returned no_results in 3ms. Both queries are well-formed natural language with concrete verbs ('add', 'lock', 'pyproject', 'uv.lock'). Returning empty after 3ms is a query-pipeline failure mode, not a corpus gap. Add a final-tier rescue: if the candidate set is empty after RRF + dense filtering, re-run dense-only with full raw query string. This is a structural fix and helps any future too-short-after-stopwords case, not just these two probes.

additionalObservations: FLOW category is catastrophic (0/8 PASS): multi-file flow-tracing queries are not currently a strength. Both no_results probes (FLOW-1, FLOW-4) and several wrong-file probes (FLOW-2, FLOW-5, FLOW-7) suggest within-crate disambiguation needs work before adding more 2-hop budget.

DEF category remains strong (6/8 PASS, 75%) — definition queries are the natural strength. UV-DEF-1 and UV-DEF-4 are both pure symbol-name-collision failures (Cache/CacheArgs, Resolver/Resolution) that the symbol-exact boost in fix #1 directly addresses.

Stop-words filter is innocent: 'how' is in QUERY_SCAFFOLD_STOPWORDS but 'trace' is not, and the query still has many content tokens (uv, add, dependency, pyproject, toml). The no_results outcome is more likely an RRF-floor or dedup problem than literal stop-word stripping.

Two probe-design issues (UV-NL-6 too-narrow symbol set, UV-ERR-2 def-vs-construction-site) account for 2 of 20 graded failures. With those reclassified, true retrieval failure count drops from 20 to 18.
